newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW tackling problem of excess workforce.
newsitem.headline: VW tackling problem of excess workforce.

text.p: Volkswagen AG said on Monday that as many as 500 positions at the carmaker may not be necessary in the next two years, particularly in its administrative areas.
A VW spokesman said the carmaker was in talks with its works council to discuss measures to reduce its workforce without resorting to layoffs.
"There are no jobs at danger in the short-term," VW spokesman Peter Schlelein said, noting the number of jobs at risk totalled about 500.

Schlelein confirmed that workers in the adminstrative offices of VW's plant No. 1 in Wolfsburg would return as of April 1 to a 28.8-hour work week from the current level of about 32 hours on a four-day schedule.
He said the move was part of normal measures at the carmaker, which is the largest in Europe, as part of wage contracts.
